name: Saint Stephen of Hungary
history: The first king of Hungary, crowned around the year 1000. Baptised as a boy, Stephen built the Church in his country, founded dioceses and monasteries, gave laws shaped by the Gospel and cared personally for the poor. Before he died he entrusted his kingdom to the Virgin Mary.
life: Stephen was born Vajk, son of Géza, chief prince of the Magyars, a people who had settled in the Carpathian basin a century before. He was baptised as a boy and married Gisela, sister of the future Emperor Saint Henry II. When Géza died, Stephen put down rebellion and in about the year 1000 was crowned king, by tradition with a crown sent by Pope Sylvester II. He founded the archdiocese of Esztergom and other sees, built churches, supported the abbey of Pannonhalma and welcomed missionaries. His laws protected widows and orphans, and he was known to give alms in disguise. His deep grief was the death of his only surviving son, Saint Emeric, in a hunting accident in 1031. Having no heir, Stephen offered Hungary to Our Lady. He died on the feast of the Assumption in 1038 and was canonised in 1083. His right hand is venerated in Budapest.
prayerTo: Saint Stephen, you ruled your people as a Christian king and entrusted your kingdom to the Mother of God. Pray for all who govern, that they may seek justice and protect the weak. Pray for parents who have lost children, and for me, that I may give God the first place in all I do. Amen.
penance: Pray today for those who hold public office, and give alms quietly to someone in need.
meditation: In the counsels he wrote for his son, Stephen urged him to be patient and merciful, and to rule as a servant of Christ. Whom has God placed in your care, and how are you serving them?
